newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends limit up on stepped up cash trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends limit up on stepped up cash trade.

text.p: Reports of increased cash trade continued to provide support and CME lumber futures closed up as much as their $10.00 limit on local demand, traders said.
Lumber closed limit up to $0.60 higher, with July limit up at $362.40 per tbf and September $7.70 higher at $354.20.

Futures turned around from Wednesday's losses that come on fund selling on reports from cash sources that cash trade picked up late Wednesday and higher prices being paid for eastern spruce studs, they said.
"The market is showing some signs of improving here and there," said Curt Cunningham, President of Pacific Futures Trading.

But Cunningham said there has not been enough improvement in the cash market to justify a limit rally in futures. There has been some improvment but most of the run up in futures came from local demand. Even though cash activity is up, cash is generally trading at the lows for the week, he said.
The market may also be using forest fires in Canada for a reason to run futures higher, Cunningham added.
Cash spruce prices recently broke to $350 per tbf, the lowest price since July 12, 1996.
